BiblicalUsage: If brethren dwell together, and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger, and if the man like not to take his brother's wife, then let his brother's wife go up to the gate.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the brother-in-law's duty is the law's way of refusing to let a name die: the dead man's line is carried by the living brother, and the gate hears the case when the brother will not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
